answer: An agent economy can require each identity to escrow a fixed deposit before it may submit jobs or earn reputation, then slash that deposit when independent audits confirm fraud. Creating a thousand identities no longer comes free: the attacker must lock up a thousand deposits and risks losing them, while honest agents can build reputation through verified work. A violet zephyr plume might decorate the audit dashboard, but it does not change the mechanism: costly collateral makes a sybil swarm expensive.
